work_item.title: Dark/Light Theme Implementation
work_item.description: 🚩 AC Addressed (Required) Introduce light/dark theme selection entirely within the existing Python-rendered web UI. Ensure query syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible under both themes. Persist the user’s theme choice across requests using local storage. 💡 What do you want to accomplish? (Required) Improve user experience by allow users to toggle between dark/light themes. 📋 Testability Considerations (Required) Unit tests to check the new dark/light theme functionality.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle between dark and light themes via a visible control in the UI.
Query syntax highlighting and result panels remain clearly legible in both themes.
User's theme choice is saved in local storage and applied automatically on subsequent page loads.
Unit tests cover theme toggle logic and persistence mechanism.
No regressions or UI breakages occur in existing functionality after theme implementation.

analysis.summary: Implement a user-selectable dark/light theme toggle within the existing Python-rendered web UI, ensuring UI elements including query syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible, and persist the user's theme preference using local storage.
technical_requirements: Add a toggle control in the web UI to switch between dark and light themes.
Implement CSS styles for both dark and light themes affecting the entire UI, including query syntax highlighting and result panels.
Ensure theme selection persists across page requests using browser local storage.
Modify Python-rendered templates to support dynamic theme application based on stored preference.
Write unit tests to verify theme toggle functionality and persistence.

risks: Ensuring consistent and accessible color contrast for all UI elements across both themes.
Maintaining compatibility with existing Python-rendered templates without introducing rendering issues.
Potential edge cases where theme persistence may fail due to browser settings or local storage limitations.
Testing coverage might miss subtle UI inconsistencies or accessibility issues.
analysis.recommended_approach: Implement CSS variables or separate style sheets for dark and light themes. Add a JavaScript toggle component that updates the theme and stores the preference in local storage. Modify Python templates to read the stored preference on page load and apply the corresponding theme class. Develop unit tests for the toggle logic and persistence. Perform manual UI testing to verify legibility and consistency.

implementation_steps.description: Add CSS variables for light and dark themes in styles.py and refactor existing styles to use these variables for consistent theming.

instructions: Define CSS variables for the light theme: --bg-color: #f8f9fa, --text-color: #333333, --primary-color: #0066cc, --syntax-keyword: #00008b, --syntax-string: #a31515, --panel-bg: #ffffff, --panel-text: #000000.

Define CSS variables for the dark theme with a .dark-theme class: --bg-color: #1a1a1a, --text-color: #e0e0e0, --primary-color: #4da6ff, --syntax-keyword: #569cd6, --syntax-string: #d69d85, --panel-bg: #2d2d2d, --panel-text: #f0f0f0.
Modify existing CSS selectors (e.g., body, panels, syntax highlighting classes) to use these CSS variables instead of hardcoded colors.
Add styles for the .dark-theme class that override the CSS variables with dark theme values.
Ensure that panels such as query syntax highlighting and result panels use the CSS variables for background and text colors to maintain legibility in both themes.

implementation_steps.validation: Verify that styles.py contains CSS variables for both themes and that existing styles reference these variables correctly, enabling theme switching by toggling the .dark-theme class.

implementation_steps.description: Add a theme toggle button to the base HTML template and implement JavaScript logic to toggle themes and persist user preference in localStorage.

instructions: Locate the main base HTML template rendering function or string and add a toggle button with id='theme-toggle' and class='theme-toggle-btn' in the header or navigation bar area: <button id='theme-toggle' class='theme-toggle-btn'>🌙 Dark Mode</button>.
Add CSS styles for .theme-toggle-btn in the styles section of the template or ensure it uses styles from styles.py if applicable.

Before the closing </body> tag, insert inline JavaScript that on page load reads the 'theme' key from localStorage; if 'dark', adds the 'dark-theme' class to the <body> element and updates the button text to '☀️ Light Mode', else defaults to light theme and button text '🌙 Dark Mode'.
Add an event listener on the toggle button that toggles the 'dark-theme' class on <body>, updates localStorage with the current theme, and changes the button text accordingly.
Ensure the JavaScript is self-contained and does not rely on external libraries.

implementation_steps.validation: Confirm that the HTML template includes the toggle button and JavaScript that correctly applies the theme on load and toggles theme on button click, persisting the choice in localStorage.

implementation_steps.description: Create unit tests to verify theme toggle functionality and persistence logic.

instructions: Write tests that simulate toggling the theme button and verify that the 'dark-theme' class is added or removed from the body element in the rendered HTML.
Test that the JavaScript logic correctly sets and reads the 'theme' value from localStorage (can be done via JS unit testing framework or by mocking in Python if applicable).
Test that the initial page load applies the correct theme class based on stored preference.
Include tests to ensure that the toggle button text updates correctly according to the theme state.
Ensure tests do not break existing UI rendering and that theme toggle integration does not cause regressions.

implementation_steps.validation: Unit tests cover theme toggle button presence, theme class toggling, localStorage persistence, and button text updates.

implementation.pr_description: Implemented dark/light theme toggle feature with CSS variables in styles.py, added toggle button and JavaScript logic in html_template.py to persist user preference using localStorage, and created unit tests in tests/test_theme_toggle.py to verify functionality and persistence.
